scope: Only eight latency_cold/latency_slow rows and their native lookup/export metadata; no response-body or allocation-journal repeat.
finding: All eight rows lack a matched same-key native complete-read/export result in their own epoch. Seven directories have only four files and empty export-event journals. PID1062 has a real completed export job for the later changed-source stage, but no native read result for base key1. Those changed bytes cannot attest its earlier base-source slow request. This is an evidence gap, not proof that the cache actually failed.

targetedProspectiveDirection.boundary: After each selected successful protected response and observed origin/gateway settlement, before the next destructive clear/context change. Perform the complete observation before starting the next timed request. Do not overlap any measured request interval or alter the original started/first-response-byte/finished timestamps.
targetedProspectiveDirection.exactProbe: Use the existing explicit native TSCacheRead exporter on the original request's exact key/lookupURL, same PID/startTicks/source/version/user/ACL. Preserve the actual accepted/finished events, result/body/source-Slice equality and any NO_DOC/error/timeout. A successful read is bounded read-time readability of the complete relevant Slice; not whole64MiB or physical disk durability.
targetedProspectiveDirection.artifact: Separate raw request-linked sidecar, never a seventh lifecycle stage or an invented successful measurement.
targetedProspectiveDirection.actualInstrumentationCounts: Nine extra native export jobs are a targeted candidate, not already observed. Each of the first eight affected server epochs had zero export jobs, while PID1062 had one; the proposed additional one stays within existing8-job/16-control/512MiB per-epoch exporter budgets for these exact target rows. Future code must check real remaining budget rather than assume it.
targetedProspectiveDirection.accounting: All additional native read/retained pool backing, Python two fixed export/reference slots and hash/control memory remain in the full closed-window and original8MiB accounting. Observational file I/O is not a capacity exemption or a timing/throughput acceptance claim.
targetedProspectiveDirection.failure: A missing key, context drift, active request, insufficient native budget, NO_DOC, short body, mismatched bytes or failed read must remain actual failure/unproven and must not be turned into true canonical flags.
targetedProspectiveDirection.doNotGeneralize: Do not blindly add a job for every one of101 rows or every success; that can exceed the existing native process budgets. This addendum proves only these eight plus the previously reviewed first-miss gap, not universal coverage of all other canonical request flags.
